summary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): Bogotá Capital District: the best-documented trans community and services in the country, alongside a documented police-violence pattern in its tolerance zone. Regional evidence: Red Comunitaria Trans reported police shouting at, baton-beating and shooting at trans sex workers at 3:50 a.m. on a central street (the district mayor's office took up the case); two trans women were killed within hours of each other on the night of 2 January 2026 (a 24-year-old in Engativá, a 20-year-old in Florida Blanca); a 32-year-old trans activist was found dead in the eastern hills in December 2023, with the press itself framing 'the recurring mechanisms in crimes against trans women'. The district's own law journal published a study of violence against trans people in the Santa Fe tolerance zone, where sector expulsions push people into other localities. Mass identity-check operations: 200+ officers in San Bernardo (April 2025) and over 1,200 uniformed officers with background and migrant control in Santa Fe (January 2026) - a visibly gender-nonconforming person in central Bogotá is therefore statistically likely to be in the path of a sweep. Scored relative to the national score (0.52) for Colombia.

sources.summary: El País in English (April 14, 2025): the transphobic murder that shocked the country - Sara Millerey, 32, a trans woman, beaten and thrown into a creek in Bello (Antioquia) on 4 April 2025; national context: 13 trans people killed in Q1 2025, presidential call to investigate, vigils in several cities. Cited in this record as national lethal-violence context.
